sections.bio:
I have been working in SEO and digital marketing since 2009, specializing in Local SEO, AI SEO, Google Maps SEO, lead generation, and multi-location search visibility for businesses throughout the United States.

I originally founded Professional Lists, Inc., where I developed digital marketing systems focused on client acquisition, organic search growth, email marketing, paid advertising, and lead generation strategies. In 2022, I transitioned operations into SEO Company Santa Monica LLC with a stronger focus on Local SEO, AI SEO, and Google Maps ranking strategies for competitive local markets.

Over the years, I have helped businesses improve rankings, increase inbound leads, and generate measurable growth through:
• Local SEO
• AI SEO
• Google Maps SEO
• Google Business Profile Optimization
• Multi-Location SEO
• Content Strategy
• Website Optimization
• Citation Building

My company currently ranks in top search results for competitive keywords including:

I work with local businesses, service companies, and multi-location brands looking to improve online visibility, increase calls and bookings, strengthen local authority, and generate long-term organic growth.

Experience includes:

I focus on practical SEO strategies that generate measurable business results rather than vanity metrics, helping businesses convert local search traffic into customers, calls, leads, and long-term revenue growth.

Update on my Google Maps SEO case study:
Google Maps still generates calls.
Even with AI Overviews, AI search, ChatGPT, Perplexity, and all the changes happening in search, local customers are still using Google Maps when they need a business now.
They are looking for:
A phone number
Directions
Reviews
A nearby provider
A business they can call immediately
That is why Google Maps SEO still matters.
In this campaign, the business went from 0% Share of Local Voice to 72% Share of Local Voice in under 30 days.
The improvement did not come from one simple Google Business Profile edit.
It came from aligning the full local SEO foundation:
Google Business Profile optimization
Geo-relevance
Citation consistency
Local landing page support
Mobile page speed
Prominence and trust signals
Website and GBP alignment
The biggest lesson is that Google Maps rankings are not only about being close to the searcher.
They are about being relevant, trusted, and visible across the area where customers are searching.
AI search is changing discovery, but Google Maps is still one of the strongest conversion channels for local businesses because it connects visibility directly to phone calls, directions, and customer action.
Full case study:
https://lnkd.in/gQYbBmgF
Reddit discussion:

Recently, I communicated with a service provider that had a nice website, strong branding, and what looked like an impressive system.
But when I started asking basic buying questions, the representative could not clearly explain what the company actually did or how their system worked.
That experience reminded me of a simple sales lesson:
Sell the sizzle, not the steak.
A website can create interest, but clear communication creates trust.
I wrote more about this in my latest article.
Read it here:

I just shared a Google Maps SEO case study showing how a local campaign improved from 0% to 72% Share of Local Voice in about 30 days.
The strategy was not based on keyword stuffing or random SEO tactics.
It came down to aligning the core local SEO signals that Google actually uses:
Geo-relevance
Citation consistency
Google Business Profile optimization
Local landing page support
Mobile page speed
Prominence and trust signals
The biggest takeaway was that the improvement was not just one keyword moving up. The entire map grid improved across the surrounding area.
That is what matters in Google Maps SEO.
Ranking at the business address is one thing. Expanding visibility across the area where real customers are searching is where the opportunity is.
I also referenced Google’s own local ranking documentation around relevance, distance, and prominence because those principles still matter.
For anyone working on local SEO, Google Maps rankings, or multi-location visibility, this case study is a good example of why foundational SEO still drives results.
